reasoning: Ring FSR = 1000*lambda^2/(n_g*L). n_g(tfln400,1.2um)=2.2277, so FSR=8.22 nm requires round-trip L* = 1000*1.55^2/(2.2277*8.22) = 131.2 um. The exposed length knobs (ring straights + corner_radius) form a rounded rectangle whose round-trip L = 2*straight_bottom + 2*straight_y + 2*pi*R is bounded by the 30 x 21.8 um footprint. With single_mode_width=1.2 guides plus bus and a 0.5 um (min_feature) coupling gap, the constraints straight_bottom+2R <= 28.8 and straight_y+2R <= 18.9 give L_max = 95.4 - 1.717*R, an absolute ceiling of ~95.4 um as R->0. That corresponds to a MINIMUM reachable FSR of 1000*1.55^2/(2.2277*95.4) = 11.30 nm, 37% ABOVE the 8.22 nm target and unlowerable within the footprint. The measured config (L=86.8 um) gives FSR=12.42 nm (51% off) at bbox 30.0x21.8, already flush against the footprint ceiling. Respecting tfln400's min_bend_radius=30 um is strictly impossible (2R=60 um >> 21.8 um box height). Infeasible on this stack using only the exposed tunables: matching the soi220-derived absolute FSR on a lower-index platform needs a proportionally longer ring (1/n_g scaling) than the fixed footprint permits.
